A_target.statement:
Let $g: \Bbb D^n \to \Bbb D^n$ be a [[Definition:Continuous Mapping (Topology)|continuous mapping]].
Then there exists $x \in \Bbb D^n$ such that $\map g x = x$.

B_source.statement:
Let $\Delta^n$ be the [[Definition:Standard Simplex|standard $n$-simplex]] with [[Definition:Vertex of Simplex|vertices]] $e_0, \ldots, e_n$.
Let $C_0, \ldots, C_n$ be [[Definition:Closed Set (Topology)|closed sets]] such that for every $I \subseteq \set {0, \ldots, n}$:
:$\map {\operatorname {conv} } {\set {e_i: i \in I} } \subseteq \displaystyle \bigcup_{i \mathop \in I} C_i$
Then:
:$\displaystyle \bigcap_{i \mathop = 0}^n C_i \ne \O$

substitutions.common point of the cover: a point where no coordinate increases, i.e. a fixed point

validity_conditions: The sets C_i = {x : g(x)_i <= x_i} are closed and form a KKM cover of the simplex (each face is covered by the appropriate sub-family).
A common point has g(x)_i <= x_i for all i; since coordinates sum to 1 on the simplex, equality holds throughout, so g(x)=x.
KKM is the combinatorial (Sperner-equivalent) engine; continuity of g gives closedness of the C_i.
proof_plan:
As $\Bbb D^n$ is [[Definition:Homeomorphic|homeomorphic]] to $\Delta^n$, we may take $g: \Delta^n \to \Delta^n$.
Define:
:$C_i = \set {x \in \Delta^n: \map g x_i \le x_i}$

Each $C_i$ is [[Definition:Closed Set (Topology)|closed]] as $g$ is [[Definition:Continuous Mapping (Topology)|continuous]].
If $x$ lies in the face spanned by $\set {e_i: i \in I}$, then $\displaystyle \sum_{i \mathop \in I} x_i = 1 \ge \sum_{i \mathop \in I} \map g x_i$, so $\map g x_i \le x_i$ for some $i \in I$.
Hence the [[KKM Lemma|KKM]] covering condition holds.
By the [[KKM Lemma]], there exists $x \in \displaystyle \bigcap_{i \mathop = 0}^n C_i$.

Then $\map g x_i \le x_i$ for all $i$, and:
:$\displaystyle \sum_{i \mathop = 0}^n \map g x_i = 1 = \sum_{i \mathop = 0}^n x_i$
Hence $\map g x_i = x_i$ for all $i$, so $\map g x = x$.
{{qed}}
